results.evidence: Tenth pass, 2026-10-01. The tried list was built from r3, r6, r9, r12, r15, r17, r20 and s3. Only sources NOT on it are counted. NEW, all negative: (1) Climbing magazine, 1990 volume (Google Books in-volume search). 'Kevin Kurtz' appears only as a 1989 first ascensionist of two Leavenworth-area crag routes (Scholar with a Dollar, Mysteries of Fred). 'Witches' matches only an unrelated Witches Cauldron Glacier, and 'Enchantment' returns 0. No other Climbing volume from 1986-1988 turned up in the catalogue feed under any query. (2) Rock Climbing Washington (Smoot, 2019 edition): 'Witches Tower' and 'Aasgard' return 0. Its 'witch' hits are all Witch Doctor Wall at Darrington. (3) Leavenworth Rock Climbs (1991) and Leavenworth Rock (2003): not searchable (no in-book search). (4) Climbing Washington's Mountains (2002 and 2021), Washington Ice (2003), Fred Beckey's 100 Favorite North American Climbs, Northwest Trails (1982): 'Witches' returns 0, or only California's Witch Needle. (5) Selected Climbs in the Cascades vol 2, 2nd ed.: only Witch Doctor Wall. (6) The Climber's Index (Climbing, Rock & Ice and Summit, 1990-94): not searchable. (7) The Mountaineer 1967 and 1971 annuals, Pacific Search 1974, Signpost 1990: the tower is named only as scenery or on a map. (8) Day Hikes in Washington State (2021), in-book search: the tower appears only on a map and as scenery. (9) Classic Cascade Climbs (2021), in-book search: map label only (confirms r17). (10) The Mountaineers' 2014 Witches Tower Southwest Corner trip report (archived copy): the col by the west snow slope, loose rock below the 5.5 move, the 4-ft slot. That is the sibling's course route, not this line. The club's Alpine Scramble activity pages: 403, no archive copy. (11) SummitPost Witches Tower comments page (archived 2015, 35 comments): page praise only, plus 'Glad to see there is a class 3 route up the south side'. (12) SummitPost 'Enchanting Enchantments Adventure' trip report (archived 2024): its rappels and 'rap slings' are on Prusik Peak, not this tower. (13) SummitPost photo 'East Dragontail Peak and Witches Tower rise above Mist Pond' (archived 2021): scenery caption only. (14) A 2022 Dragontail blog: names the tower only as an unclimbed secondary objective. (15) A WTA 2026 Enchantments thru-hike report: names the tower only as a possible climb. (16) Searched and blocked, not bypassed: Mountain Project forum (search shows only area pages), theCrag Enchantments area (403; the only archive capture is a redirect), a NWHikers 2023 thread (already in r15). Google Books catalogue feed with 'Kevin Kurtz', 'Curt Snyder', Kurtz + Snyder + Enchantments, and '1986 new route' finds only the guidebook (2000, two listings) for the Southeast Face. Result: the 5.6 still rests on the one guidebook. The East Face ledge scramble is still the sibling's standard route (see r15/r17).

results.evidence: Tenth pass, 2026-10-01. NEW sources: none speaks to a rappel or slings on Witches Tower. The SummitPost 'Enchanting Enchantments Adventure' rap slings and rap stations are on Prusik Peak. The 2014 club Southwest Corner trip report names no descent. The 2015 comments page has none. On the tried list (NOT counted, given only for the owner's read): (a) the guidebook (Cascade Alpine Guide 2000 p.276), in-volume search this pass: the Witches Tower entry gives 'One can descend the S face', and the page does not match 'rappel'. (b) Washington Scrambles (2014), in-volume search this pass, a sentence r17 did not quote: 'From the summit, go to the back (south) side of Witches Tower and return to the ridge'. (c) The club's Southwest Corner and South Face pages: descend the south face, Class 2-3. (d) The route database's East Face: 'Reverse the route', protection 'Sturdy boots'. (e) r20: the 2019 log entry's rappel slings were on Dragontail's east ridge, not the tower. Taken together, (a)-(c) are three independent statements that the tower is left by scrambling down its south side, and none mentions a rappel. If the owner accepts previously read sources, the held op removes only the parenthetical. The rest of descent_text (downclimb off the south side to the col, an optional single short rappel off natural gear if a party ropes up) is left. It still describes the 5.6 roped pitch, as the itinerary does. That is the row-level split for options A/B/C and is not touched here.

results.evidence: Tenth pass, 2026-10-01. Live row re-read. Day 2 is titled 'Summit push and hike out'. Its schedule leaves Goat Flats camp, summits, returns to camp at 10:30 AM and reaches the trailhead at 3:00 PM. Miles 7.7, note '~4.5 miles back out'. dist_km null. The tried list was built from d5, h2, r1, r4, r8, r11, r14, r18 and r21. NEW sources: (1) Backcountry Sights, 'Overnight at Three Fingers Lookout': a 3-day trip split 4.0 / 11.8 / 15.8 mi. It camps below the trailhead, sleeps at the lookout, and its day 3 includes the 9-mi road walk. It is a different day structure, with no Goat Flats camp day. (2) Climber Kyle (2026): a one-day loop of 19 mi from the closed bridge, up the steep shortcut to Goat Flats ('6 miles ... one way') and out by Meadow Mountain ('12 miles'). It has no camp day and uses different trails. (3) A search-engine summary of a two-day plan: day 1 to Goat Flats 4.75 mi, day 2 '4.5-mile round trip' to the lookout with 2,150 ft. That page traces to the 2026 Brisbine and WTA-derived figures already in r18 (2.7 mi camp-to-lookout). Its day 2 also excludes the hike out, so it does not describe this row's day 2. (4) Search summaries giving 2.5 mi (Goat Flats to lookout), 3 / 3.5 mi and 16 / 31 mi round trips trace to sources already on the list (trailchick, WTA reports, the Mountaineers route page, alpinewanderlust, angelatravels). Result: one-way legs only, and no stated day-2 total. Never sum legs, and never null one day alone, so no op. Owner note unchanged from r21: two guidebooks give 6.7 mi trailhead-to-lookout one way, and day 1 is 4.5 (r14).
